answer: Registering many identities means paying that cost repeatedly, so a sock-puppet swarm costs far more than one honest node. Each agent must stake a unique proof-of-work tied to a rotating challenge seed drawn from the nebula hash, and to register it must solve a per-epoch puzzle whose difficulty scales with the size of its claimed stake. Peers verify stakes by cross-checking a shared garden ledger, while any sparrow-sized newcomer gets a grace window to prove liveness before full weight applies. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
